eyebrow: Built for Rwanda's community health workers
heroBody: ZeroMalaria helps community health workers assess malaria risk, identify danger signs early, and refer patients to the health centre, including when offline.
problemTitle: The referral loop breaks between the village and the clinic.
problem1B: Danger-sign checks vary from one visit to the next.
problem2B: A paper slip leaves the village and is never confirmed.
problem3B: Districts see surges and stock-outs after the week they needed to act.
how1B: One question at a time: age, fever, danger signs, RDT. Works fully offline.
how2B: Clinical rules decide urgency. The health worker reviews and confirms.
how3B: A digital referral with QR code reaches the health centre inbox.
how4B: If the patient never arrives, the health worker is alerted to follow up.
whoChwB: Guided triage in the village, in Kinyarwanda, with voice.
whoSupB: Team, patients and follow-ups for one facility.
whoRbcB: Live map, surge signals, referral funnel, stock pressure.
safetyTitle: AI assists. Clinical rules decide. People confirm.
layer1B: Danger signs always mean urgent referral. Never downgraded.
layer2B: May only raise urgency, never lower it, and explains why.
layer3B: Helps with words and voice. Never diagnoses, never names drugs.
voiceTitle: Speaks Kinyarwanda. Listens for yes or no.
voiceBody: Questions are read aloud from a fixed, reviewed phrase catalogue, so the health worker can keep their eyes on the patient.
offlineBody: Every assessment is saved locally and syncs automatically when the network returns.
ctaTitle: Zero malaria deaths starts in the village.
ctaBody: Sign in with the account provided by your administrator.
footerBuilt: AI for Public Good Hackathon · University of Rwanda · UR UNIPOD
